original_target.title: Non-explosion of Brownian Fleming–Viot systems in arbitrary domains
original_target.outcome: Claim: negative: finite-time Brownian branching explosion

answer: Negative: a bounded connected three-dimensional driftless Brownian explosion domain.
required_status_qualification: Solved on the basis of an unverified announcement. The full target is claimed in the cited source; the external proof has not been independently verified here.
scope_comparison: Theorem1.1 supplies for every N>=3 a bounded connected open Omega_N in R3 and positive probability of tau_infty<T for every interior configuration and T>0. Taking N=3 suffices to refute the universal d,D,N,x assertion. The §2/§7 model is standard driftless Brownian motion with uniform survivor copying; auxiliary operational drift is removed by a common time change preserving the joint Brownian/donor law. Boundary holes accumulating at the explosion point are permitted because the target has no regularity condition. Earlier flawed unrestricted proof and N=2 positive theorem do not limit this announced N>=3 counterexample.
